x: …beat us by the small margin of two points, our lads took a very good share of the prizes and all walked extremely well. G. Coleman, of Highgate, showed that he is maintaining his fast times, beating Harry Churcher by 23 seconds.…
At this point, George Coleman had a few yards' advantage over the Belgrave trio, Gregory, Churcher and McMullen—well stimulated by the exhortations of numerous "Bels" supporters.
We had twenty-four starters for this event and the uphill climb was taken easily by our lads, but towards the turn they had moved up into better positions. At the turn G.

Belgrave men, it seemed, were everywhere, and if all had been eligible to score we would have won the team event; as it was we missed third place by one point and were only eight points behind Metropolitan Walking Club, the winners. George Coleman added to his list of triumphs and missed the course record held by R.
